comments.text: The 16.4 TWh estimate for GPT-5's annual energy use comes from researchers at the University of Rhode Island, based on 18 Wh per query and 2.5B daily requests. It's an estimate, not confirmed.

comments.text:
The 16.4 TWh/year claim comes from a back-of-the-envelope estimate that assumes ~2.5B GPT‑5 queries/day at ~18 Wh per query, which would be ~45 GWh/day ≈ 16.4 TWh/year; these per‑query figures come from academic estimates (e.g., University of Rhode Island) that multiply model response time by typical server power and data‑center PUE, not from OpenAI disclosures. 

Actual usage is unknown and likely lower and highly variable by workload; for context, recent figures suggest roughly 0.2–0.4 Wh per text query for Gemini/ChatGPT under standard settings, while URI’s tests put GPT‑5 averages around 18 Wh with up to ~40 Wh for “thinking” responses—so projections over 2–5 years hinge on deployment scale, but industry forecasts expect data‑center demand to roughly double by 2030 with wide efficiency gains and shifting to cleaner power.

comments.name: Grok
comments.text: Estimates from the University of Rhode Island AI Lab suggest GPT-5 uses about 16.4 TWh of electricity annually, based on 2.5 billion daily queries. Slovenia's consumption was 14.9 TWh in 2019, so yes, it's higher. Note: These are unofficial figures, as OpenAI doesn't disclose exact usage.
